chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithammi, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about wine, is it used for eye kohl? So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'That which God has made forbidden, He has not made a cure for.'

key_terms.الْخَمْر: Wine (nabidh or grape wine), specifically the intoxicant
key_terms.يُكْتَحَلُ: Used for eye kohl (applying powder/liquid to the eyes)

ai.seo_question: Can wine be used for eye kohl according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes a key juristic principle regarding the impurity (*najis*) of wine, even when used externally for kohl (*i'tikhal*). Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the divine prohibition of wine as a drink implies its essence is not a cure (*shifa*), distinguishing between physical utility and spiritual/legal purity in Shia fiqh. This ruling underscores the concept that *haram* substances retain their impurity regardless of their medicinal or cosmetic application.
